contractCoverage.contract: 1. Sensitive web-search query is never presented to any cmux/browser surface, and provider selection (including explicit provider choice) is preserved
contractCoverage.evidence: web/search/index.ts: executeSearch no longer accepts or calls `presentation?.presentResearch({kind:'query',...})` (removed entirely, confirmed by diff and a repo-wide grep for `presentResearch(` finding only the URL-shaped call site in tools/fetch.ts). `CmuxResearchPresenter.presentResearch` signature changed to `(url: string, signal?)` — a query string can no longer be passed even by mistake. `params.provider` is still passed straight through unmodified to `resolveProviderChain` (comment: 'Coalescing to auto here would silently bypass that preference'). CmuxPresentationAdapter test asserts no call argument ever contains 'google.com'. Web-search CLI (`web-search-cli.ts`) no longer imports/creates a cmux presentation object at all.

contractCoverage.contract: 2. redactUrlForPresentation strips query string, fragment, and userinfo; returns null for credentialed/non-http(s) URLs
contractCoverage.evidence: fetch.ts: `redactUrlForPresentation` returns `${url.origin}${url.pathname}` only, rejects url.username/url.password, and rejects non-http(s) protocols. Unit test `redactUrlForPresentation` (fetch-insane-fallback.test.ts) verifies: X-Amz-Signature query stripped, #token fragment stripped, alice:password@ URL -> null, file:// -> null, malformed string -> null. Confirmed passing (part of the 141-test run).

contractCoverage.contract: 3. cmux tab titles built from a subagent progress event carrying secrets contain only controlled agent/tool tokens, never free text/descriptions/URLs/secrets
contractCoverage.evidence: cmux/integration.ts: `ProgressLike` interface only has id/status/agent/currentTool (description/task/recentOutput fields removed from the type entirely); `#progressText` only reads `progress.agent`/`progress.currentTool`, each filtered through `safeSurfaceToken` (regex `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9 ._:/-]{0,63}$`, rejecting anything with `=`, `://`, spaces-only free text patterns that don't match the identifier grammar). Test 'never projects raw output, descriptions, or secrets into tab titles' feeds a progress payload with description/task/recentOutput containing X-Amz-Signature, a postgres credentialed URL, and 'token'/'password' strings, then asserts the resulting rename-tab title contains only 'executor' and 'Tool: web_search' and none of the secret substrings. Confirmed passing.

contractCoverage.contract: 4a. A never-settling or slow presenter cannot block, delay, or fail the primary read (bounded by signal + hard deadline)
contractCoverage.evidence: fetch.ts: `presentResearchBounded` races `presenter.presentResearch(...)` (swallowing rejections) against a `setTimeout` capped at `Math.max(250, deadlineMs)`, called from `renderUrl` with `deadlineMs = Math.min(timeout*1000, 2000)`. QA red-team test (ad hoc, this run): a presenter whose `presentResearch` returns a promise that never resolves or rejects still let `ReadTool.execute` complete in 2.21s and return the fetched content, proving the read is not blocked.

contractCoverage.contract: 4b. defaultRunner kills the spawned cmux CLI child process on abort/timeout instead of leaking it
contractCoverage.evidence: cmux/integration.ts `defaultRunner`: attaches a `setTimeout(kill, timeoutMs)` and an abort listener that both call `kill()` (which calls `process.kill()` and marks `terminated`), returning exitCode 124 on either path; listeners/timers are cleaned up in a `finally`. Verified by static code read only in this pass (spawning/killing a real child process was intentionally not exercised live to avoid touching the workstation's process/cmux environment); this matches the pattern already covered indirectly by the adapter's mocked-runner circuit-breaker tests.

contractCoverage.contract: 5. Default-off `cmux.presentation` setting means no presentation activity without opt-in
contractCoverage.evidence: config/settings-schema.ts: `cmux.presentation` has `default: false`. sdk/session.ts only constructs `CmuxPresentationAdapter`/`CmuxProjectionSubscription` when `!isCanonicalSubSession && settings.get('cmux.presentation') === true`. tools/fetch.ts `renderUrl` only calls `presentResearchBounded` when `presenter && settings.get('cmux.presentation') === true`. QA red-team test (ad hoc, this run): with the setting left unset, `settings.get('cmux.presentation')` reads `false` and a spy presenter's `presentResearch` was never invoked during a successful read.

contractCoverage.contract: 6. An aborted signal makes tryInsaneFallback throw (propagate ToolAbortError) rather than swallow the abort as an ordinary failure
contractCoverage.evidence: tools/fetch.ts `tryInsaneFallback` now has two explicit `if (args.signal?.aborted) throw new ToolAbortError();` guards (before and after `routeInsanePublicUrl`). Unit test 'propagates abort instead of swallowing it as an ordinary failure' pre-aborts an AbortController and asserts `tryInsaneFallback(...)` rejects. Confirmed passing.

contractCoverage.contract: 7a. renderHtmlToText low-quality rejection restored (short/JS-gated/nav-heavy content is not treated as a successful native render)
contractCoverage.evidence: tools/fetch.ts `renderHtmlToText` now gates success on `content.trim().length > 100 && !isLowQualityOutput(content)` (previously only checked `content.trim()` truthiness). A caller with genuinely low-quality rendered HTML now correctly falls through to the Insane/llms.txt/document-extraction fallback chain in `renderUrl` instead of being returned as a false-positive success. Confirmed by direct diff read and passing `fetch.test.ts`/`fetch-insane-fallback.test.ts` (existing renderUrl integration coverage for the JS-gated/low-quality fallback branch).

contractCoverage.contract: 7b. Insane search provider handles text queries via keyless DuckDuckGo discovery (not just direct URL routing)
contractCoverage.evidence: web/search/providers/insane.ts `searchInsane`: for a non-URL text query, calls `searchDuckDuckGo({ query: discoveryQuery(params.query), ... })` for keyless discovery, then routes each discovered candidate URL through the same guarded `routeInsanePublicUrl` path, deduplicating and capping at `numResults`; falls closed with a clear `SearchProviderError` when nothing routes. Test 'routes discovered public URLs for non-URL text queries' (query 'reddit test' resolves via DuckDuckGo HTML scrape -> reddit RSS route) and 'emits a diagnostic when configured Insane falls back to DuckDuckGo' both pass; 'rejects unsupported URLs instead of unsafe generic browsing' confirms direct URL-shaped queries still fail closed without DuckDuckGo discovery (read path stays direct-URL-only, no generic browsing bypass).

webSearchPresentationRemoval.evidence: src/web/search/index.ts, src/web/search/providers/insane.ts, src/cli/web-search-cli.ts — no cmux presentation seam remains in the search path; `getSearchTools()`/`webSearchCustomTool` no longer accept a presenter argument; `runSearchCommand` no longer creates or disposes a `CmuxInvocationPresentation`.

urlReadPresentationBounding.evidence: src/tools/fetch.ts — `redactUrlForPresentation` + `presentResearchBounded` gate cmux presentation for URL reads behind default-off `cmux.presentation`, origin+pathname-only redaction, and a signal+deadline race; verified statically and via ad hoc QA tests in this run.

cmuxTabTitleProjection.evidence: src/cmux/integration.ts — `CmuxProjectionSubscription`/`safeSurfaceToken`/`ProgressLike` restrict tab-title content to identifier-shaped agent/tool tokens only; covered by the existing 'never projects raw output, descriptions, or secrets into tab titles' unit test.

insaneFallbackAbortAndGating.evidence: src/tools/fetch.ts `tryInsaneFallback`/`classifyInsaneFallback`/`getInsaneFallbackOutcome` — abort propagation, raw/disabled/unsupported/401/forbidden/non-transient gating, and cmuxVerified gating all covered by fetch-insane-fallback.test.ts (30 assertions, all passing).

insaneSearchDiscovery.evidence: src/web/search/providers/insane.ts — DuckDuckGo-backed discovery for text queries restored alongside direct-URL routing and fail-closed behavior for unsupported/unroutable targets; covered by web-search-insane.test.ts (19 assertions, all passing).
